data.name: Miraya
data.gender_notes: Miraya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'mira' which means delight or enchantment. The name Miraya is often used in Hindu mythology to refer to the divine enchantress, Mohini, who used her powers of illusion and charm to save the world from destruction. The name Miraya carries the meaning “Delight, Enchantment, Charm” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Miraya usually hope their child will grow to embody delight, enchantment, charm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radiates divine charm and allure, attracting good fortune and blessings.
data.etymology: Miraya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delight, Enchantment, Charm.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Miraya total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Miraya holds significant cultural value in Hinduism, as it is reminiscent of the divine enchantress Mohini. She played a crucial role in Hindu mythology by using her powers of both enchantment and illusion to save the world from certain destruction during the cosmic battle between good and evil. The name carries an essence of charm, allure, and captivation, reflecting the remarkable abilities of Miraya, also known as Mohini, in Hindu lore.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Miraya holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism. The Sanskrit root 'mira' implies delight or enchantment, and the name is associated with the enchantress Mohini. The spiritual essence of the name is rooted in the connection between beauty, allure, and the divine, representing the power of illusion and transformation. The name calls to mind the divine Hindu deity and the ability to transform one's inner self through spiritual practices to achieve enlightenment and ultimate happiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Miraya represents the enlightened inner observer, the one who watches the play of life from a detached yet compassionate perspective. It symbolizes the awakened consciousness that transcends the limitations of the physical world, enabling one to perceive the underlying unity and interconnectedness of all things.

vedic_reference.note: Miraya is mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Ramayana as a friend of the gods. She is also considered an incarnation of the goddess Lakshmi.

historical_references.reference: Miraya is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of Indra's horse. Miraya is described as being white, swift, strong, and having the ability to traverse the sky and underwater realms.

In Hindu mythology, Miraya is also the name of a demoness who was the mother of the demon Mahishasura. According to legend, she was cursed by a sage for disrespecting him, and as a result, she gave birth to Mahishasura who wreaked havoc on the gods until he was eventually slain by the goddess Durga.
